why: It sells by weight and it produces during the night, so it needs the kitchen of the restaurant and the costing of the retail sector at the same time.
operator: The owner is in the shop at four in the morning while the first batch bakes, then at the counter at seven with the queue of the commuters. Their pain is the weight and the price: the customer asks for three quarters of a kilo and the shop has to be fast and exact. The second pain is yesterday bread: it is good food on the second day and a loss on the third, and the owner decides the discount by feel.
entities: Bakery (id, name, branchId, address, phone, currency, openingHours, taxRegistration)
Product (id, sku, nameAr, nameEn, categoryId, unit, unitPricePiasters, costPiasters, taxRate, isWeighed, isBatch, shelfLifeDays)
ProductionBatch (id, productId, producedAt, quantity, costPiasters, expiresAt, status, note)
Sale (id, branchId, cashierId, lines, totalsPiasters, payments, createdAt, idempotencyKey)
SaleLine (id, saleId, productId, quantity, weightGrams, unitPricePiasters, discountPiasters, isWeighed)
Waste (id, productId, productionBatchId, quantity, reason, loggedBy, createdAt)
PurchaseOrder (id, supplierId, status, lines, expectedAt, totalPiasters)
Shift (id, branchId, openedBy, openedAt, closedAt, floatPiasters, countedPiasters)
Employee (id, name, phone, role, station, hourlyRatePiasters, status)
StockItem (id, nameAr, unit, costPiasters, quantity, supplierId, reorderPoint)
units: piece, kilo, gram, portion, pack, tray, dozen, with the weight sold per kilogram and the pastries sold per piece
batches: Yes for everything made in house: each production batch carries the date, the quantity, the cost of the ingredients and the expiry, so the owner knows what yesterday bread cost him
expiry: The day old rules are per product: the shelf life, the day it becomes discounted and the day it is written off. The screen shows the batches that expire today with the quantity, and one tap writes them off with a reason
special: The structures specific to this sector are the production batches from the night shift, the weight based selling with the scale, the daily price changes for a holiday or a promotion, and the day old discount rule
screens: Weighed till: the pastries and the bread by the weight, with the scale value and the price per kilogram, and the quick keys for the most sold items
Production plan: what the night shift bakes, how much, and what was actually produced against the plan
Day old screen: the batches that expire today, the quantity, and the discount rule or the write off
Stock: the flour, the sugar, the butter, the fillings and the packaging, with the last count and the reorder point
Daily price: change the price of an item for today only, with the reason written in the audit log
Purchasing: the order to the supplier with the last price and the quantity
Shift and the end of day: the money counted, the waste of the day in money and the number of pieces sold
roles: Owner: everything, including the prices and the staff
Manager: everything except billing, approves the write offs and the price changes
Baker: the production plan and the batches, no cash
Cashier: the counter, the scale, the payment and the shift close
Assistant: the counter and the stock count, no price change
reports: Sales by product and by hour: the morning rush measured
Day old waste in money per day: the loss the owner never measured
Margin per product after the real batch cost
Production against the plan: what was baked and what was sold
Stock of the raw material with the days left
integrations: Weighing scale through the local bridge or WebSerial, with a manual weight entry as a fallback
Thermal printer through ESC/POS for the receipt and for the batch label with the date
Camera scanner on the phone for the stock count of the flour and the packaging
WhatsApp for the order confirmation and for the day old offer to the regulars through the bakery own account
onboarding: Business basics: name, branch, address, phone, currency, opening hours
Products: the items the shop sells, with the ones sold by weight marked
Shelf life: the number of days each item stays fresh, and the rule for the day old discount
Raw material: the flour, the sugar, the butter and the packaging with the counts
Team: the baker, the cashier and the assistant
Suppliers: the main suppliers with the visit days
First week plan: weigh one item, produce one batch, close the shift, set the day old rule
seed: Category list in Arabic: عيش, معجنات, بيتزا, كيك, حلويات, بسكويت, كرواسون, سندويتشات
A weight and piece unit set with the price per kilogram
A shelf life list per category as a starting point, marked to be confirmed by the shop
A receipt layout with the weight line and the production date for the items that are made in house
Role templates for the baker, the cashier and the assistant

landing_en.headline: A bakery that sells by weight and knows what yesterday bread cost
landing_en.sub: A till with the scale, night production batches, and a day old rule you set once
benefits: The weight comes from the scale and the price per kilo is on the screen
The night batch is recorded with its date, its quantity and its cost
The day old discount rule is set once and applies itself
faq: Is the day old bread thrown away? It is converted by the rule before it becomes waste, and the rule decides the discount day
Does it work with a broken connection? Yes: the till keeps selling and the receipt prints from the device

pricing: The free tier fits a small bakery with one counter: one business, one branch, two seats, the weighed till and the shift
Starter adds the production plan, the day old rule and a year of history
The Business tier adds the purchasing, the raw material stock and the waste report
The kiosk for the self service bread shelf is priced per device

tasks.title: Register the bakery pack in the sector registry
tasks.brief: Add the manifest for bakery in packages/core/src/sectors/registry.ts with the base template restaurant and the mix of retail modules (pos, weights, production, expiry, purchasing, shifts), the feature flags, the role templates and the terminology map.
tasks.done: getSector('bakery') returns the manifest and the registry test asserts the modules and the flags.

tasks.title: Write the bakery data model with the production batches
tasks.brief: Type the entities in packages/core/src/sectors/bakery/schema.ts: products with the weighed flag and the shelf life, production batches with the date, the quantity and the cost, daily prices with a reason, the waste log and the sale lines with the weight in grams.
tasks.done: The schema compiles with no any, the validation rejects a sale of a product without a production batch when the category requires one, and the tests pass.

tasks.title: Build the bakery seed with the Arabic categories and the shelf lives
tasks.brief: Write packages/core/src/sectors/bakery/seed.ts with the Arabic categories, the weight and piece units, the shelf life per category marked as a starting point to confirm, the receipt layout with the weight line and the production date, and the role templates.
tasks.done: The seed loads, the test asserts the categories and the shelf lives, and it asserts that no price was invented.

tasks.title: Write the bakery terminology map in Arabic and English
tasks.brief: Create packages/ui/src/sector/bakery/glossary.ts with the trade words: عيش, معجنات, دفعة, اليوم التاني, خصم, وزن, and the counter words, in Arabic and English.
tasks.done: The glossary covers every screen of the sector with no generic shop wording and the label test passes.

tasks.title: Build the weighed till and the scale driver
tasks.brief: Build the weight based sale: the cashier presses the weight button, the scale value lands in the line in grams, the price per kilogram multiplies it, and the manual entry stays available when the scale does not answer.
tasks.done: A weighed sale stores the grams and the price matches the scale value, the simulated driver test passes, and a manual weight is accepted and marked as manual.

tasks.title: Build the production plan and the night batches
tasks.brief: Build the screen where the night shift records what it baked: the product, the quantity, the ingredients cost and the expiry, and the comparison with what was sold during the day.
tasks.done: A batch records the production date and the expiry, the plan against the sale comparison matches a manual count in the test, and the batch label prints with the date.

tasks.title: Build the day old screen with the discount rule
tasks.brief: Build the day old screen: the batches that expire today with the quantity, the rule for the discount day, one tap to apply the discount and one tap to write off with a reason, each written to the audit log.
tasks.done: The batches due today are listed with their quantities, the discount rule applies the right percentage, the write off reduces the stock and both actions are audited.

tasks.title: Build the raw material stock and the purchasing
tasks.brief: Build the stock of the flour, the sugar, the butter, the fillings and the packaging with the last count and the reorder point, and the order to the supplier with the last price.
tasks.done: The low stock list names the items below their reorder point with the last purchase price, and the order prints with the quantity and the price.

tasks.title: Build the bakery report pack
tasks.brief: Add the reports of this sector: sales by product and by hour, the day old waste in money, the margin per product after the real batch cost, the production against the plan, the raw material stock and the cash reconciliation, each with the CSV export.
tasks.done: Every report computes its own numbers, the test matches a manual calculation and the export opens in a spreadsheet.

tasks.title: Publish the bakery landing page in Arabic and English
tasks.brief: Build the sector page from the outline: the Arabic headline first, the weighed till and the day old screen as the proof blocks with real screenshots, the two questions answered, and the English mirror.
tasks.done: The page passes the layout rules at 320 to 1920 px in both languages and both themes, and every claim matches a screen that exists.

risks: The shelf life list is a starting point and the shop must confirm it from the real product, because a wrong shelf life is a food safety question
The scale is the source of the price, so the manual entry is always available and marked as manual in the receipt
The day old rule never disposes stock on its own without the owner seeing the amount and pressing the button
Allergen labelling is the shop own text: the product never decides that an item is safe for someone
